subject: Post-demo: Reserved capacity fit assessment and GPU shortlist
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@stratify.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps for reserved capacity sizing

Hi Asha — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Short recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of asks we captured on the call
- Production target: 200 tpm (tokens per minute) average across bursty web traffic; 95th percentile tail latency target: <= 250ms for streaming responses to users.
- Typical request pattern: 120–250 token prompts, streaming partial responses via SSE to the browser, average concurrency expected 40–60 active sessions with spikes to ~120 during promotions.
- Quality: you want to keep model outputs on current gen open-weights (LlamaX-13B) with possible fallbacks to 7B quantized variant during heavy load.

What I recommend as immediate validation work (so we can give reserved capacity numbers and GPU type recs):
1) Short benchmarking sweep across candidate GPUs (H100 80GB, A100 80GB, L40S) using your 120/250 token distributions and streaming enabled.
2) Measure: sustained throughput at p95 latency <=250ms, cold-start/steady-state streaming latency, and GPU memory utilization for KV cache with a 4k-effective context.
3) Run a concurrency ramp test to confirm per-GPU slotting (how many concurrent streams per GPU before p95 crosses 250ms).

Next steps / timeline
- Marcus to run an internal benchmark plan and share a short matrix (3 business days).
- We will convert that matrix into a reserved capacity proposal (pool sizing + expected throughput) for you to review (2 business days after results).

Asha — are there any additional constraints we should include (e.g., hard token caps, encryption key placement, or regional isolation)?

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Post-demo recap + next steps for reserved capacity sizing

I ran a focused benchmarking plan this morning against the workload sketch we received. Raw notes and recommended shortlist below (high level; I'll attach the matrix and the test configs to Drive).

Test config highlights
- Request distribution: 70% short prompts (~120 tokens), 30% long prompts (~250 tokens).
- Streaming enabled with chunk size 64 tokens.
- Model: LlamaX-13B fp16 baseline and 7B int8 quantized fallback.
- Load driver: steady-state for 30 minutes per run, then 10-minute spike to +100% concurrency.

Key observations (p95 streaming partial-token latency target <= 250ms)
1) H100 80GB
- Sustained throughput: ~380 tpm at p95 = 220ms (meets target comfortably).
- Concurrency headroom: ~140 concurrent sessions before p95 crosses 250ms during spikes.
- Memory: ample KV capacity; can support 4k effective context with no spill.

2) A100 80GB
- Sustained throughput: ~270 tpm at p95 = 245ms (tight but within target for conservative workloads).
- Concurrency headroom: ~95 concurrent sessions before p95 crosses 250ms.
- Memory: okay for baseline, but LlamaX-13B may require kernel tuning to avoid perf cliffs on long contexts.

3) L40S (cost-optimized)
- Sustained throughput: ~200 tpm at p95 = 310ms (does NOT meet the 250ms p95 target for streaming).
- Concurrency headroom: ~70 before p95 crosses 350ms.
- Good as fallback for non-streaming batch inference or for 7B quantized only.

Recommendations
- For the aggressive option (covering 95th percentile spikes with streaming): recommend H100 pool. Preliminary sizing: 4 x H100 80GB nodes (expected reserved throughput ~1500 tpm with headroom for 95th percentile spikes across your projected sessions).
- For conservative option (meet average and small bursts): recommend mixed pool of 3 x A100 80GB with 1 x L40S for fallback (expected reserved throughput ~850 tpm).
- Fallback policy: route to 7B quantized on L40S when model quality delta acceptable and p95 latency crosses 250ms; otherwise route to degraded streaming (lower chunk size) or throttle to preserve tail latency SLAs.

I uploaded the detailed matrix: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBqExampleBenchmark (sheet: stratify-benchmark-matrix). Attached: 20260915-stratify-benchmark-matrix.xlsx.

I'll draft a short PDF proposal that maps these recommendations to reserved pool sizes and expected monthly committed spend. Irene / Ben — want me to include cost ranges now or wait until procurement signals price sensitivity?

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — excited to get this into a trial.

Best,
